authors: Yang Ying, Qu Yihao, Cao Limei and Yang Ji
abstract: Ruthenium dioxide (RuO2) is a highly active catalyst for the acidic oxygen evolution reaction (OER), but its anodic dissolution limits long-term operation. Here, we synthesized a series of YxRu1−xO2 catalysts and identified Y–RuO2–2 as the best-performing composition among the samples tested in a three-electrode cell containing 0.1 M HClO4. Y–RuO2–2 requires an <mark>overpotential</mark> of 206 mV to reach 10 mA cm−2 and remains operational during a 345 600 s (96 h) chronopotentiometry test.
